cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 4537 (Internet Software Architecture) is a 3-credit course that focuses on the design, development, management, and security of web APIs, with a strong emphasis on RESTful architectures.

Here is a breakdown of what the course covers:

*   **Core Concepts:** You will explore RESTful APIs, their relationship with HTTP, CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations, REST constraints, and the use of HTTP status codes.
*   **Practical Skills:** Students learn to design simple web services, develop programs using REST, JSON, and HTTP, write API specifications, and implement error handling.
*   **Security and Management:** The course covers securing backend API servers, applying change management, and versioning designed APIs.
*   **Prerequisites:** To enroll, you must have completed COMP 1537 and COMP 3522.
*   **Program Integration:** This course is offered as part of the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
* https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/

cases.question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.standalone_question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 1113 (Applied Mathematics) is divided into three main topic areas designed to build a strong foundation for your future programming and technical courses. 

The three main topic areas are:

*   **Boolean Algebra and Logic Circuit Design:** You will learn about Boolean concepts (such as TRUE/FALSE values, operators, and theorems), construct truth tables, work with canonical forms (SOP and POS), and simplify expressions using Karnaugh maps. You will also apply these concepts to design practical logic circuits like adders, comparators, and decoders.
*   **Number Systems and Data Representation:** This section covers positional number systems and how computers represent numbers, text, and graphics internally. You will practice arithmetic operations across different bases (binary, octal, and hexadecimal) and study various computer representations, including 1s and 2s complement, BCD, and floating-point representation.
*   **Functions, Linear Equations, Vectors, and Matrices:** You will study how to solve systems of linear equations with up to three variables using algebraic methods, matrices, and determinants (Cramer’s rule). This area also covers basic matrix operations such as addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, multiplication, and finding the inverse of a matrix.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/courses/applied-mathematics-comp-1113/
* https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261048068/
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/

cases.question: By how much can BCIT raise domestic tuition each year, and when do the new rates take effect?

cases.answer_excerpt:
BCIT can raise domestic tuition by up to 2 percent each year, and the new rates take effect on August 1.

Here are the details regarding domestic tuition increases:

* **Annual Increase Limit:** In accordance with the provincial government's Tuition Limit Policy, BCIT and other BC post-secondary institutions are permitted to increase domestic tuition by a maximum of 2% annually.
* **Effective Date:** BCIT posts the newly approved tuition rates in April of each year, and they officially take effect on August 1 for the upcoming academic year. 
* **Paying in Advance:** If you pay your tuition before the new rates are posted in April using the older rates, you will be required to pay the difference within 10 business days from the start of your program.

cases.question: Does BCIT offer on-campus student housing at the Burnaby campus?
cases.standalone_question: Does BCIT offer on-campus student housing at the Burnaby campus?
cases.answer_excerpt:
Yes, BCIT offers on-campus student housing at the Burnaby campus. 

BCIT provides over 800 student rooms directly on its Burnaby campus. The available housing options include:

* **Tall Timber Student Housing:** Opened in Fall 2025, this 12-storey sustainable mass timber building provides 469 beds. It features fully self-contained studio suites, private rooms with shared bathrooms and kitchens (Connected Single rooms), and collaborative spaces. Priority access is given to Indigenous students and former youth in care.
* **Legacy Townhouses:** These accommodate 12 students per townhouse in private rooms with shared common facilities.

### Eligibility and Location
* **Eligibility:** International students accepted into a full-time, cohort-based BCIT program are eligible to apply for student housing. 
* **Location:** The Burnaby campus housing is centrally located between Brentwood Town Centre and Metrotown, offering easy access to transit, shopping, and dining.

Students are advised to apply for housing as early as possible.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/student-services/student-life-housing/
* https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/guides/housing-guide/
* https://www.bcit.ca/about/leadership-vision/history/
